```{python}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import sys

# add parent directory to path as this is where the functions are stored
sys.path.append("..")
# import functions 
import functions as fn

```


Load in the data
```{python}

df_com = pd.read_csv("Data/Hormone_time_series_data_interpolated.csv")

num = fn.df_to_numpy(df_com, "Cortisol")

common_t = df_com["NewTime"].iloc[0:72].values

df_meta = pd.read_csv("Data/redcap_controls.csv")

```


# Perform PCA on cortisol time series data

```{python}

pca = PCA(n_components=10)
pca_res = pca.fit(num)


```


# Make Figure of PCA results

First extract the wake, lunch and dinner times from the metadata.

According to the readme - 'Metadata is recoded by participants over 3 days. Hormone sampling typically started in the morning of day 2 and therefore ends 24hrs later in the morning of day 3'

```{python}


# get wake times
wake_times= fn.to_integer_wake_time(pd.to_datetime(df_meta['night2_final_wake']).dt.time)

# Lunch time
lunch_times = fn.to_integer_wake_time(pd.to_datetime(df_meta['day2_lunch_time_v2']).dt.time)

dinner_times = fn.to_integer_wake_time(pd.to_datetime(df_meta['day2_dinner_time_v2']).dt.time)
dinner_times[dinner_times == 0] = np.nan

```


```{python}

pc_to_plot = [0,5,6] # note these are off by one due to python zero indexing

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2,2,figsize=(14, 10))

ax = ax.flatten()

# plot the selected PCA components
for i in range(len(pc_to_plot)):
    ax[i].plot(common_t,pca_res.components_[pc_to_plot[i],:])
    ax[i].set_title(f"PC {pc_to_plot[i]+1}")
    ax[i].set_xlabel("Time")
    ax[i].set_xticks(np.arange(720, 2160+240, 240), ['12', '16', '20', '24', '04', '08','12'])
    ax[i].set_ylabel("Loading")


y = np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.38, len(wake_times))
ax[0].plot(wake_times + 24*60,y, 'ro', label="Wake time", alpha = 0.25) # Since wake times are on second day we add 24 hours to the time
ax[1].plot(dinner_times, y, 'bo', label="Dinner time", alpha = 0.25) # Since dinner times are on second day we add 24 hours to the time
ax[2].plot(lunch_times , y, 'go', label="Lunch time", alpha = 0.25) # Since lunch times are on second day we add 24 hours to the time


# In last box plot cumulative explained variance
pc_sum =  np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_)
ax[3].plot(np.arange(1,11,1),pc_sum, marker='o', color = 'black')
ax[3].set_xticks(np.arange(1,11,1))
ax[3].set_title("Explained variance of PCA components")
ax[3].set_xlabel("PC")
ax[3].set_ylabel("Cumulative explained variance")
ax[3].set_ylim(0,1)
ax[3].set_xlim(0.75,10.25)
ax[3].hlines(y = pc_sum[-1], xmin = 0, xmax = 10, color='red', linestyle='--', label='Total explained variance')
ax[3].set_yticks([0.0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,0.93,1.0])

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```


# Explained variance of PCs

```{python}



plt.plot(np.arange(1,11), np.cumsum(pca.explained_variance_ratio_), marker='o')
plt.title("Explained variance of PCA components")
plt.xlabel("Principal component")
plt.ylabel("Cumulative explained variance")

```





# Suplimentary figure - All PCA components

```{python}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(5,2,figsize=(13, 15), sharey=True, sharex=True)

ax = ax.flatten()
for i in range(10):
    ax[i].plot(common_t,pca_res.components_[i,:])
    ax[i].set_title(f"PC {i+1}")
    if i >7:
      ax[i].set_xlabel("Time")
      ax[i].set_xticks(np.arange(720, 2160+240, 240), ['12', '16', '20', '24', '04', '08','12'])


```
